description: Hi everyone! My name is Eva, and i'm from SMK Riam. I enjoy storytelling and coding, and I love exploring new ideas and bringing my creativity to life. i'm looking for creative and passionate team members  who enjoy storytelling, arts and multimedia, or graphic design. In our team, you'll have the freedom to express your creativity, share your ideas, and explore new possibilities without fear of judgement. Everyone's ideas are welcome, and we can learn from one another.
summary: For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge we built an interactive storytelling project called Abandoned but not Forgotten that brings real discarded space hardware back to life for young learners. Instead of treating old lunar and Martian machines like junk we follow two young space explorers named Maya and Sam as they visit actual historic artifacts like the Apollo 11 retroreflector and the stuck Spirit rover. This project addresses the challenge by turning technical engineering data into an engaging narrative that is easy for school age kids to understand without feeling childish or boring. It solves the problem of dry science textbooks by showing how broken parts and dead batteries still made massive scientific history like measuring the moon drifting away or discovering ancient Martian hot springs. It is important because it shifts the focus of space exploration from just flashy rocket launches to the lasting resilience of silent hardware. By connecting real landing sites to an interactive classroom map and printable mission cards we spark genuine curiosity and prove to the next generation that even abandoned machines can keep teaching us secrets about the universe.
details: Our project works by transforming real NASA mission data from silent hardware on the Moon and Mars into an accessible visual story that school age learners can easily follow and explore. It benefits middle school students and teachers by removing heavy technical jargon and replacing boring textbook dates with relatable human curiosity. Our intended impact is to spark long term interest in space exploration by proving that missions do not end when a rover stops moving. To build everything, our team kept things simple and accessible by using Notepad to write and organize our storyline and drafts, and Canva to design the visual layout and graphics. What makes our project truly creative is how it flips the typical space narrative by celebrating broken wheels, dusty solar panels, and snapped rotor blades as heroic clues that unlocked major scientific discoveries. When designing the experience, our team carefully considered scientific accuracy, age appropriate vocabulary, logical space safety like proper astronaut suits, and visual clarity so any young student could connect with the real history waiting in the dust.
